{"type":"text","timestamp":1794627664045,"sessionID":"ses_e27dccb85ffeTrBEvupZJCwTlZ","part":{"id":"prt_1d824f8a4001yUFxPipgGgCG4U","messageID":"msg_1d824dbe2001OwWMDMJXzs3Epi","sessionID":"ses_e27dccb85ffeTrBEvupZJCwTlZ","type":"text","text":"The mission failed and scores 0. The battery ran out at tick 29, about 1.7 m from base. I sampled every target, but under the scoring rules a dead battery cancels all of it.\n\n**What went well**\n- All five original targets (t1–t5) were sampled before their deadlines.\n- Both targets discovered mid-mission were sampled too, but late, so each would have earned only 25% of its value. d2 appeared with a deadline I could no longer reach, and commands I had already sent kept me from reaching d1 in time.\n- Navigation through the delay worked. I measured slip on bedrock at about 2–4% from the odometry and predicted the rover's position ahead of the old telemetry. Every sample attempt succeeded.\n\n**What went wrong**\nI never added up the energy budget, and the plan cost far more than 100:\n- Waiting cost: 0.5 per tick × 50 ticks = 25.\n- Driving: about 70 m at 1 per metre = 70.\n- Samples: 7 × 3 = 21.\n\nThat totals about 116. I didn't check until tick 24, when the battery read 21.5. By then the remaining drives and the last sample were already queued and couldn't be cancelled. After tick 26 the rover had 1.38 left, which only covered about three more ticks of waiting.\n\n**What I should have done**\nBudget energy at the start. Leave out the far, low-value t1 (worth 1) and possibly one of the late discoveries. That keeps total use under about 95 and gets the rover home with most of the value: roughly 8 points out of a possible 12, instead of 0.","time":{"start":1794627664036,"end":1794627664043}}}
